family.tagline: Two dads, two kids, and a calendar that keeps up.
family.story: Tunde is a civil-service planner who plans the family week too. Rafael flies a regional route, so some nights he is not home. Sade and Leo fill the house with piano and questions.

companion.name: Maren
companion.job: Turns the family's week of messages into one calendar Tunde edits.
companion.limits: Proposes a calendar. Tunde confirms every date.

companion.name: Gus
companion.job: Opens AirTrail in its own browser and logs each flight Rafael names.
companion.limits: Logs what Rafael names. He checks the entry.

members.name: Sade
members.work: school, piano in the living room

popup.title: Two flights up with a parcel
popup.body: The parcel waits at the top of two flights of stone steps. Rafael carries it through the foyer and the dining room to the living room.

popup.title: Sade holds the guide
popup.body: Sade holds the quick-start guide. Tunde lifts out the Companion Core, a power cable and a recovery USB drive. The footprint is about three quarters of a sheet of paper.

popup.title: Plug it in
popup.body: Tunde plugs in the cable and presses the button as Leo counts down from ten. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Rafael joins from his phone
popup.body: Rafael joins the Core's own network from his phone. Then he picks the home network from the list.

popup.title: Pick your first agents and apps
popup.body: In Companion Hub, Tunde picks Hermes and Companion Memory (beta). Rafael picks OpenClaw. They add Companion Planning, HomeHub, Navidrome and AirTrail, then walk away.

beats.capability: talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Maren says hello
popup.body: Tunde messages the agent he named Maren. Maren answers, and the Core is running.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: tunde
say.text: Hello, Tunde. Maren here. What is on the calendar?

beats.capability: talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Maren drafts the week
popup.body: Tunde texts Maren the week's school and club messages. Maren drafts one plan. Tunde edits it and enters it in Companion Planning himself.

say.speaker: tunde
say.text: Draft week ready. Please correct the dates.

beats.capability: plan tasks and time blocks in one local file on your Core

popup.title: One week, one local file
popup.body: Tunde blocks out Rafael's early routes, swim club and piano in Companion Planning. The whole week is one local file on the Core.

beats.capability: log your flights and see your whole travel history on a world map

popup.title: Gus logs the week's flights
popup.body: Rafael names the week's flights. Gus opens AirTrail in its own browser and logs each one. Rafael checks the entries on the map.

say.speaker: rafael
say.text: Flights logged. Please check the map.

beats.capability: a shared grocery list, recipe book, meal planner and expense tracker for the household

popup.title: Sunday's batch-cook, planned
popup.body: Tunde plans the batch-cook in KitchenOwl at the breakfast bar. The meal planner and the shopping list live in the same app.

beats.capability: a shared household hub for notes, shopping, chores and expenses, with a recipe book

popup.title: Leo waters the herbs
popup.body: Tunde posts the week's chores in HomeHub. Sade sets the table, Leo waters the herbs, and each tick shows on every phone in the house.

beats.capability: one start page for every app on your Core

popup.title: One start page for the house
popup.body: Tunde pins every family app to one Homarr page. Anyone on the home Wi-Fi opens the calendar, the chores and the music from the same place.

beats.capability: stream your own music collection to any device

popup.title: Sade's practice track
popup.body: From the couch, Rafael plays the backing track for Sade's piano piece from Navidrome. It streams from the Core, and she plays along.

beats.capability: turn habits and chores into a game with levels and quests

popup.title: Practice, turned into a quest
popup.body: Sade ticks off today's piano practice in Habitica. Each tick earns her character a level, and the game runs on the Core.

beats.capability: back up, search and organise your family photos and videos on your own Core

popup.title: Leo's birthday, backed up
popup.body: Tunde backs up Leo's birthday photos to Immich from the loveseat. They land on the Core, ready to search.

beats.capability: block ads, trackers and bad domains for every device on your network at the DNS level

popup.title: Ads blocked house-wide, at DNS
popup.body: Tunde checks the Pi-hole list beside the Core. Ads and trackers are blocked at the DNS level for every phone, tablet and laptop on the Wi-Fi.

beats.capability: keep a service history, fuel log and reminders for every vehicle

popup.title: Every vehicle gets a service log
popup.body: Rafael logs the car's next service and the bicycle's new chain in LubeLogger. A reminder is set before each one is due.

beats.capability: stream your own music collection to any device

popup.title: The same playlist, every night
popup.body: Tunde starts the bedtime playlist in Navidrome, whether Rafael is flying or home. It streams the family's own music to the bedrooms from the Core.

beats.capability: assign and track household chores and recurring tasks, with NFC tag completion

popup.title: A tag on the bedroom door
popup.body: Sade taps the family phone on the tag by the bedroom door when her school bag is packed. Donetick ticks the chore, and Tunde sees the tick.

beats.capability: listen to your audiobooks and podcasts, and pick up where you left off on any device

popup.title: Leo's story, where he left off
popup.body: Leo picks up his story where he stopped last night. Audiobookshelf remembers the place, on any device in the house.

beats.capability: archive the receipts, warranties and contracts you rarely look at, until you need them

popup.title: Uniform receipts, filed for good
popup.body: Rafael files the uniform receipts and a new suitcase's warranty card in Papra at the bedroom desk. They stay put until he needs them.

beats.capability: save places on a map and plan multi-day trips with a budget

popup.title: The summer road trip, mapped
popup.body: Tunde and Rafael plan the summer road trip on the outdoor sofa. TRIP saves the places on a map and keeps the budget beside them.

beats.capability: draw logos, diagrams and line art as vector graphics, in your browser

popup.title: A lemonade sign, drawn at home
popup.body: Sade draws a sign for her lemonade stand in Inkscape on the terrace. The vector file sits on the Core.

popup.title: Four people, one calendar, one Core
popup.body: Two dads, two children, and a week that keeps moving. The Adeyemi-Castro household runs on one Companion Core in the living room.

closing.body: Your calendar, your playlists and your photos can live on a Companion Core at home. Start with one shared week in Companion Planning.

notes: Owner sign-off open: the FTUE hotspot flow is written as the owner specified and is not on the fact sheet (STORY-BIBLE section 15, item 1).
Told like any other family. The kids' data is the stake, so no beat claims child safety, monitoring or learning outcomes: Habitica, Audiobookshelf and Inkscape are everyday moments.
No TV: the media beats are Navidrome and Immich at the couch. Mealie (signature) has no QA screenshot, so KitchenOwl carries the food beat and HomeHub the chores.

dining-draft: Hermes drafts and Tunde enters the plan himself, because Companion Planning has a UI link only. Companion Planning has a Google Calendar sync that is off by default; the text claims only a local file.

bed-playlist: "whether Rafael is flying or home" implies no control from away. Music Assistant was dropped (the validator bans the word assistant). bed-bag is the Donetick iot beat; its outside notifications go unmentioned.
living-dns: Pi-hole blocks at DNS and is not parental control (catalog caveat); the text never mentions the children. garage-service assumes the family owns a car; the scene shows only a bicycle.
Voice-over lexicon: Adeyemi, Castro, Tunde, Rafael, Sade (shah-DAY), Leo, Maren, Gus, Fallow Point, Foxglove, Homarr, Habitica, Audiobookshelf, LubeLogger, Papra, TRIP, Inkscape, AirTrail.
Street Foxglove Knoll Road and town Fallow Point are invented; the human map check is still open.
